chunks: Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding

a man who fulfilled his Tamattu', then a need presented itself to him, so he intended to go out to it. He (attend to) it. He (peace be upon him) said: 'So let him perform Ghusl for Ihram, and let him begin with the Hajj, and let him go regarding his need; and if he is not able to return to Makkah, he should go to Arafat.'

key_terms.عَرَفَاتٍ: Arafat (the plain where the main standing of Hajj takes place)
key_terms.لِلْإِحْرَامِ: For Ihram (the state of consecration for pilgrimage)
key_terms.لْيُهِلَّ: Let him begin/proclaim (the intention for Hajj)
key_terms.مُتْعَتَهُ: Tamattu' (a type of Hajj where Umrah and Hajj are performed separately with a break in Ihram)

ai.seo_question: What should a pilgrim do if they exit Ihram after Umrah but need to leave Makkah before Hajj day?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the procedure for a Mutamatti' pilgrim who, after completing the Umrah rites and exiting Ihram, must travel for a specific need. The ruling distinguishes between those who can return to Makkah to re-enter Ihram and perform Hajj from there, and those who cannot, instructing the latter to proceed directly to Arafat to fulfill the standing requirement, thereby preserving the validity of their Hajj.

en.hubeali: Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hafs Bin Al Bakhtary,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws regarding a man who fulfilled his Tumatto, then a need presented itself to him, so he intended to go out to it’. So heasws said: ‘So let him what for the Ihraam, and let him begin with the Hajj, and let him go regarding his need; and if he is not able upon the return to Makkah, he should go to Arafaat’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ibn abu ‘Umayr has narrated from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtariy who has said the following: “About

a man who completes Mut‘ah then because of a certain work wants to go out, he (the Imam) said, ‘He must take Ghusl (bath) for Ihram and say Talbiyah for al-Hajj, then go for his work and if he cannot return to Makkah he must go straight to ‘Arafat.’”
